Daily Quiz.question: ১) Who is the author of the literary work, "The Solitary Reaper"?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Solitary Reaper: 
এই কবিতাটি প্রকাশিত হয় ১৮০৭ সালে। 
কবিতায় দেখা যায়, একটা তরুনী মেয়ে স্কটল্যান্ডের গ্রামীন পরিবেশে এবং পাহাড়ী এলাকায় একাকী কাজে মগ্ন। কাজের পাশাপাশী সে করুন দু:খের গান গুনগুনিয়ে গাইছে।  

The Solitary Reaper, a poem by William Wordsworth, published in 1807 in the collection Poems, in Two Volumes.
It is a pastoral snapshot of a young woman working alone in a field in the Highlands of Scotland, singing a plaintive song in Gaelic.
“The Solitary Reaper” is made up of four octaves, primarily written in iambic tetrametre and generally following the rhyme scheme of ababccdd.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) "The Essays of Elia" is a/an:
Daily Quiz.exp:
"The Essays of Elia" is a/an - collection of essays.
-  Charles Lamb, English essayist and critic belongs to the Romantic Period, is best known for his Essays of Elia.
- It is his remarkable letters and the essays that he wrote under the pseudonym Elia for.
- Lamb’s first Elia essays were published separately in 1823; a second series appeared, as The Last Essays of Elia, in 1833.

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Who is considered an anti-romantic novelist of the Romantic period?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Jane Austen is considered an anti-romantic novelist of the Romantic period.
- She is called an anti-romantic novelist because of her stern attitude against youthful passion.

He some notable works - 
- Pride and Prejudice.
- Sense and Sensibility
- Mansfield Park
- Emma. 

Source: Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Who quoted this, "Prejudice is the child of ignorance"?
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Hazlitt
- Born: He was born in Kent, England in 1778. 
- তিনি একজন বিখ্যাত সাহিত্য সমালোচক এবং essayist ছিলেন।
- এই যুগের অপর বিখ্যাত সাহিত্যিক Charles Lamb তার বন্ধু ছিলেন।  
- এছাড়াও তিনি তার রচিত  humanistic essays এর জন্য সুপরিচিত।
- কারো কারো মতে,  William Hazlitt যুগের প্রধান সাহিত্য সমালোচক। 
- “Prejudice is the child of ignorance.” এটি তার একটি বিখ্যাত উক্তি।    

Best Works: 
- The dramatic literature of the age of Elizabeth (1820) 
- Characters of Shakespear's Plays
- Lectures on the literature of the age of Elizabeth
- The spirit of the Age (1825): ( সমসাময়িক যুগের লেখকদের গ্রন্থ সমালোচনা ) 

 

Source: Britannica.com & ABC of English Literature by Professor Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) "Adonais" is an elegy on the death of John Keats written by____
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Adonais, pastoral elegy by Percy Bysshe Shelley, written and published in 1821 to commemorate the death of his friend and fellow poet John Keats earlier that year.
- The title was probably taken from Bion’s Lament for Adonis, which Shelley had translated into English.
- Written in 55 Spenserian stanzas, Adonais is ranked with John Milton’s “Lycidas” for its purity of classical form.

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) What kind of literary work is, P.B Shelley's, "Ozymandias?"
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Ozymandias, a sonnet by Percy Bysshe Shelley, published in 1818.
- One of Shelley’s most famous short works, the poem offers an ironic commentary on the fleeting nature of power.
- It tells of a ruined statue of Ozymandias (the Greek name for Ramses II of Egypt, who reigned in the 13th century BCE), on which is inscribed, “Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!” Around the statue, “The lone and level sands stretch far away.”

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) The romantic period ended in:
Daily Quiz.exp:
- 1798 সাল থেকে 1832 সাল পর্যন্ত সময়কাল কে ইংরেজি সাহিত্যে Romantic Period হিসেবে বিবেচনা করা হয়। 
- 1798 সালে William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor এর যৌথ প্রকাশনা Lyrical Ballads এর মাধ্যমে এই যুগের সুচনা হয়।
- 1832 সালে with the first Reformation Act এর মাধ্যমে Romantic Period এর সমাপ্তি ঘটে।
- The period is also called the Revival of English Literature.

Major writers of the period - 
- William Wordsworth
- Samuel Taylor Coleridge
- Jane Austen 
- Charles lamb
- William Hazlitt
- Lord Byron 
- P.B. Shelley 
- John Keats

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) "The Marriage of Heaven and Hell" is written by
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Marriage of Heaven and Hell:
- The Marriage of Heaven and Hell is a book by the English poet and printmaker William Blake.
- It is a series of texts written in imitation of biblical prophecy but expressing Blake's own intensely personal Romantic and revolutionary beliefs.
- The work was composed between 1790 and 1793.

Willam Blake:
- Born: Nov. 28, 1757, London, England.
- Death: Aug. 12, 1827, London.
- William Blake was born over his father’s modest hosiery shop at 28 Broad Street, Golden Square, London.
- His parents were James Blake and Catherine Wright Armitage Blake.
- He is known as: engraver, artist, poet, and visionary.

Best Works:
- Songs of Innocence (1789)
- Songs of Experience (1794)
- The Book of Thel
- The French Revolution

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman and Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) William Wordsworth is known as:
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) The father of romantic age
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Wordsworth (1770 -1850)
- He is one of the major poets of the Romantic Period.
- William Wordsworth রচিত Lyrical Ballads এর প্রকাশনার মাধ্যমে Romantic Period এর সূচনা হয় বলে তাকে The father od Romantic Age বলা হয়।
- যদিও Lyrical Ballads, William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor এর যৌথ প্রকাশনা কিন্তু এই প্রকাশনায় William Wordsworth এর অবদান ছিল সর্বোচ্চ। 

তাঁর কয়েকটি উপাধি হচ্ছে - 
- Poet of Nature
- Poet of Childhood
- Lake Poet.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) The pseudonym "Elia" was used by_______.
Daily Quiz.exp:
The pseudonym "Elia" was used by - Charles Lamb. 
- Charles Lamb, English essayist and critic belongs to the Romantic Period, is best known for his Essays of Elia.
- Lamb's greatest achievements were his remarkable letters and the essays that he wrote under the pseudonym Elia for London Magazine, which was founded in 1820.
- In The Essays of Elia (1823) and The Last Essays of Elia (1833), Charles Lamb, an even more personal essayist, projects with apparent artlessness a carefully managed portrait of himself—charming, whimsical, witty, sentimental, and nostalgic.

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Which iconic novel below is written by Sir Walter Scott?
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Sir Walter Scott's early work consisted of poetic romances such as The Lady of the Lake.
- Ivanhoe, historical romance by Sir Walter Scott, published in 1819. It concerns the life of Sir Wilfred of Ivanhoe, a fictional Saxon knight.
- Despite the criticism it received because of its historical inaccuracies, the novel was one of Scott’s most popular works.

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Hours of Idleness by Lord Byron is a collection of__________.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Hours of Idleness (Volume of Poetry)
- Collection of short poems. 
- এটি তার প্রথম কবিতা। ১৯ বছর বয়সে তিনি এটা লিখেছিলেন। 
- এই গ্রন্থের অনেকগুলো কবিতাই  imitation of classic Roman poets. 
- It consists of 187 pages with thirty-nine poems.

Lord Byron:
-in full George Gordon Byron, 6th Baron Byron, (born January 22, 1788, London, England—died April 19, 1824, Missolonghi, Greece.
-British Romantic poet and satirist whose poetry and personality captured the imagination of Europe.
-This English poet revolts against existing social customs and norms. So that he is called ''The Rebel Poet''.

Best Works:
- Renowned as the “gloomy egoist” of his autobiographical poem Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage (1812–18)
- Lara,
- The Vision of Judgment,
- Hours of Idleness,
- Heaven and Earth.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) "Fanny Price" is a character from which novel written by Jane Austen?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Fanny Price" is a character from 'Mansfield Park', a novel written by Jane Austen.
- Mansfield Park, novel by Jane Austen, published in three volumes in 1814.
- its tone and discussion of religion and religious duty, it is the most serious of Austen’s novels.
- এই novel এর অন্যতম প্রধান চরিত্র তথা Female protagonist 'Fanny Price', is a self-effacing, a poor relation of timid disposition but have strong principles.
- In the novel Fanny goes to live with the family of Sir Thomas and Lady Bertram, her wealthy uncle and aunt.
- Fanny is befriended by her cousin Edmund and her moral strength eventually wins her complete acceptance by the Bertram family and marriage to Edmund Bertram himself.

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Which literary work ushered the beginning of the Romantic age in English Literature?
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
Daily Quiz.exp:
• 'Lyrical Ballads' ushered the beginning of the Romantic age in English Literature.

- 1798 সাল থেকে 1832 সাল পর্যন্ত সময়কাল কে ইংরেজি সাহিত্যে Romantic Period হিসেবে বিবেচনা করা হয়। 
- 1798 সালে William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor এর যৌথ প্রকাশনা Lyrical Ballads এর মাধ্যমে এই যুগের সুচনা হয়। 
- Lyrical Ballads এর প্রকাশনা English Literature এর উল্লেখযোগ্য পরিবর্তন এনেছিল, বিশেষত Subject and Style এর ক্ষেত্রে। 

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Lord Byron is commonly known as:
Daily Quiz.exp:
• Lord Byron, in full George Gordon Byron is a British Romantic Poet commonly known as Rebel poet of English Literature. 
- This English Poet revolts against existing social customs and norms. So that he is called 'The rebel Poet'
- His poetry and personality captured the imagination of Europe.
- Renowned as the “gloomy egoist” of his autobiographical poem Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage (1812–18) in the 19th century,
- He is now more generally esteemed for the satiric realism of Don Juan (1819–24).

Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Who wrote the poem, "Lamia"?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Lamia, narrative poem in rhymed couplets by John Keats, written in 1819.
- Lamia is the last of the four metrical romances written by Keats.
- Its source is a short anecdote in Robert Burton's Anatomy of Melancholy that Keats appended at the end of the poem.
- In the poem, Lamia and Lycius, a young man from Corinth, fall in love.
- Lamia, the poem seems to say that passionate love is an illusion and an enchantment, ultimately destructive.

Source: Cliffs Notes.
